claims.text: Pt–Pd–Au–Ag–Cu nanoparticles with minimal atomic-size mismatch form a uniform single-phase FCC structure under rapid-heating synthesis conditions.
Substitution by a closely related noble metal with a slightly different atomic radius incrementally increases the overall atomic-size mismatch.
Keeping the rapid-heating and rapid-quenching regime fixed isolates size-driven lattice strain as the only variable.
Hume–Rothery rules can predict synthesis temperatures suitable for single-phase formation in these nanoparticles.
Atomic-size disparities among the constituent elements induce local lattice strain.
Below a critical atomic-size-mismatch threshold, configurational entropy is sufficient to stabilize a uniform, low-strain FCC solid solution.
Exceeding the critical atomic-size-mismatch threshold increases the enthalpic penalty associated with local lattice strain.
The increased strain-related enthalpic penalty favors phase separation.
The increased strain-related enthalpic penalty favors elemental segregation.
The increased strain-related enthalpic penalty can produce inhomogeneous lattice parameters.
Nanoparticles with minimal atomic-size mismatch will largely retain a single uniform phase with consistent diffraction patterns.
Nanoparticles with larger atomic-size mismatch will show more phase separation or structural inhomogeneity than the initial baseline.
XRD peak splitting or broadening will accompany the predicted phase separation, inhomogeneity, or increased lattice strain.
TEM will reveal variations in local lattice parameters as atomic-size mismatch increases.
The proposed relationship applies to small-radius substitutions within the noble-metal family but not to extreme substitutions or interventions that substantially change electronic structure.

contradictions.description: The conditions claim that size-driven lattice strain is the only variable, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that substitution may also change chemical properties. Element substitution therefore does not cleanly isolate atomic size without further controls.
